prompt:
Research what the Python Software Foundation or the CPython developers have officially said about the performance impact of the free-threaded (no-GIL) build. Cite the PEP or documentation page and quote the relevant statement.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
The Python Software Foundation and CPython developers have outlined specific performance expectations and trade-offs for the free-threaded (no-GIL) build through PEP 703, PEP 779, and official documentation. The consensus is that while single-threaded performance incurs a penalty, the ability to utilize multiple CPU cores efficiently justifies the cost.

**Performance Overhead and Targets**

The Steering Council initially accepted that a performance penalty was expected, setting a loose expectation of 10-15% for the worst case. Later, PEP 779 established stricter criteria for officially supporting the free-threaded build, proposing a hard target of 15% overhead for Phase II.

SOURCE: https://discuss.python.org/t/pep-703-making-the-global-interpreter-lock-optional-in-cpython-acceptance/37075?u=hugovk | QUOTE: "At this point we’re expecting a (worst case) performance penalty of 10-15%." | CLAIM: The Steering Council initially expected a worst-case performance penalty of 10-15% for the free-threaded build.

SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0779/ | QUOTE: "For phase II (not the default flip), we propose 15% as a hard performance target." | CLAIM: PEP 779 proposes a hard performance overhead target of 15% for the free-threaded build to achieve officially supported status.

**Measured Performance Impact**

Recent measurements indicate that the actual overhead is currently around 10% on Linux and Windows, and significantly lower on macOS. The overhead varies by architecture and workload.

SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0779/ | QUOTE: "The performance penalty on linear performance, comparing a free-threaded build against a with-GIL build, as measured by the pyperformance benchmarks... is currently around 10% (except on macOS, where it’s more like 3%)." | CLAIM: Current benchmarks show a ~10% performance penalty on Linux/Windows and ~3% on macOS for single-threaded workloads.

SOURCE: https://docs.python.org/3/howto/free-threading-python.html | QUOTE: "On the pyperformance benchmark suite, the average overhead ranges from about 1% on macOS aarch64 to 8% on x86-64 Linux systems." | CLAIM: Official documentation states that average single-threaded overhead ranges from 1% on macOS aarch64 to 8% on x86-64 Linux.

SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0703/ | QUOTE: "The changes to make CPython thread-safe without the GIL increase execution overhead for `--disable-gil` builds." | CLAIM: PEP 703 acknowledges that making CPython thread-safe without the GIL inherently increases execution overhead.

**Memory Usage Trade-off**

Developers have also noted that free-threaded Python uses more memory than the standard GIL-enabled build, which is considered an acceptable cost for efficient parallelism.

SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0779/ | QUOTE: "Free-threaded Python currently sees about 15-20% higher memory use (geometric mean, as measured by pyperformance)." | CLAIM: Free-threaded Python currently exhibits 15-20% higher memory usage compared to the GIL-enabled build.

SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0779/ | QUOTE: "We propose a target of 20% (geometric mean, as measured by pyperformance) for phase II." | CLAIM: PEP 779 sets a 20% memory overhead target for the free-threaded build to be considered officially supported.

**Impact on Default Build**

It is explicitly stated that the changes required for free-threading do not negatively impact the performance of the default GIL-enabled build.

SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0703/ | QUOTE: "Note that this PEP would not affect the performance of the default (non `--disable-gil`) builds of CPython." | CLAIM: The free-threading changes do not affect the performance of the default GIL-enabled CPython builds.

SOURCE: https://discuss.python.org/t/pep-703-making-the-global-interpreter-lock-optional-in-cpython-acceptance/37075?u=hugovk | QUOTE: "The performance impact should be isolated to a free-threaded build; a GIL build should not see any performance impact in existing code." | CLAIM: The Steering Council requires that performance impacts be isolated to the free-threaded build, leaving the GIL build unaffected.
